tei:titleStmt.tei:title: 3: On my bed at night, I sought him whom my soul loves; I sough

tei:div.tei:p: On my bed at night, I sought him whom my soul loves; I sought him but did not find him. I will rise now and roam through the city, in the market places and in the streets, I will seek him whom my soul loves; I sought him but did not find him. The watchmen found me those who circle about the city; him whom my soul loves, have you seen him? Scarcely had I departed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves; I grasped him and would not let him go until I brought him to my mother's house and to the chamber of her who conceived me. I bind you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem by the gazelles and the does of the field; that you do not cause hatred nor disturb this love while it still pleases. Who is this ascending from the desert, with palm-like pillars of smoke; in a cloud of myrrh and frankincense, of all the powders of the perfume seller? Behold the bed of Shlomo, sixty mighty men are around it; of the mighty men of Israel. All of them holding swords, skilled in battle; each with his sword at his side for fear of the nights. A canopy has King Shlomo made of the wood of Lebanon. Its pillars he made of silver, its covering of gold, its curtain of purple wool; its interior bedecked with love from the daughters of Jerusalem. Go forth and gaze, daughters of Zion, upon King Shlomo; upon the crown with which his mother adorned him on the day of his wedding, and on the day his heart rejoiced.

tei:note.tei:p: During the long nights of exile, Israel seeks its former open, uninhibited relationship with God.—Alshich
Israel is determined not to sleep through the night of exile, but actively searches out every possible avenue of rapprochement with God.—Alshich

Rashi says that the ‘watchmen’ refers to Moshe and Aharon who guarded Israel from sin during the Egyptian exile. According to Alshich it also refers to Ezra and Nechemiah who were watchmen of Israel during the Babylonian exile.
Have you any word from Him? Have you been assured of His deliverance?—Rashi

Shortly after the departure (the death) of Moshe and Aharon, at the end of forty years in the wilderness, Israel saw that God was still with them as he helped them conquer the thirty one kings in the days of Yehoshua.—Rashi

Israel declares that she did not rest until she built the Tabernacle at Shiloh.—Rashi According to Alshich the verse refers to the First Temple, the dwelling place of the Shechinah, and the Second Temple which was a mere chamber compared to the Divine grandeur of the First Temple.
According to Rashi, Israel recalls when the Jews marched in the desert led by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire. (See Exodus 13:21.)
This refers to the incense offering which was offered on the Inner Altar.—Rashi

A reference to the אהֶל מוֹעֵד , the Tabernacle, and אֲרוֹן הַקוֹדֶשׁ , the Holy Ark. This is in accordance with Rashi who interprets לִשְׁלוֹמוֹ as מֶלֶךְ שֶׁהַשָׁלוֹם שֶׁלוֹ , the King to whom peace belongs. Thus, the bed of Shlomo refers to the resting place of the Divine Presence.
This refers to those who are skilled in the מִלְחַמְתּוֹ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה , the “warfare” of Torah learning.
They are always on guard lest the Torah be forgotten and troubles befall them.—Rashi
A reference to the Temple which was constructed from trees brought from Lebanon.

The interior of the Tabernacle and the Temple were arranged with objects symbolizing the love between God and Israel, such as the Ark, its cover, the Cherubim and the Tablets of the Law that were in the Ark.—Rashi
This refers to the day of the giving of the Torah when Israel crowned Him as their King and accepted His yoke.
